bodies.name: De Kamer van volksvertegenwoordigers / La Chambre des représentants (Belgian House of Representatives)
bodies.layout: A dense, functionally-driven ColdFusion (.cfm) site that reads like a legislative database front end rather than a modern marketing homepage. A slim top bar carries FAQ/Contact/Sitemap and NL/FR language-switcher links above a banner logo. Below, a horizontal dropdown mega-menu (De Kamerleden, De Kamer, Documenten, U en de Kamer, Publicaties, Bezoek ons) exposes dozens of PDF-icon-flagged sub-links to legislative registers, statistics, and archives. The body centers on a same-day session agenda strip ('DONDERDAG 2 JULI 2026') linking to a live video stream, a two-column 'NIEUWS' grid of thumbnail news items, a 'DE LEDEN' section with a hemicycle seat-distribution diagram, and a persistent full-text/database search toolbox offering four distinct search modes. The footer is a long vertical stack of icon-linked institutional shortcuts (history, library, lobby register, ethics committee, archive, whistleblower policy) plus social media icons.
ui_patterns: PDF-icon markers (pictos_pdf.gif) prefixing every document-download link across the mega-menu
same-day sitting agenda strip with direct link to live video stream ('De Kamer Live')
hemicycle seat-distribution diagram image (halfrond) visualizing party composition
four parallel search-tool variants (database search, full-text search, combined search, keyword-in-document search)
'info' icon buttons linking to PDF explainer fact-sheets next to major menu sections
sign-language interpreted question-hour announcement as a standing news tile
whistleblower policy PDF linked directly in the footer (Klokkenluiders)
NL/FR/DE trilingual switcher plus a dedicated 'Informationen auf Deutsch' footer shortcut

bodies.name: Eerste Minister van België / Premier ministre de Belgique (Prime Minister of Belgium)
bodies.layout: A minimal, Drupal 11-powered biography-and-news site personally branded to the sitting Prime Minister (Bart De Wever) rather than the institution itself, reflected in the page's own metadata title 'Bart De Wever'. A slim top strip offers NL/FR/DE/EN language links and a cross-link disclaimer pointing to the umbrella portal www.belgium.be for official services. The header centers a large portrait photo, the PM's name in oversized type, his title 'Eerste minister van België', and a row of personal social-media icons (X, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn). A compact three-item nav (Nieuws, Biografie, Contact) sits above a simple single-column 'Nieuws' feed of dated press items and a 'Samenstelling regering' block linking out to the separate federal-government composition microsite. The footer is sparse: only Persoonsgegevens (privacy) and Toegankelijkheidsverklaring (accessibility statement) links plus a repeated Belgian 'be' logo mark and high-contrast toggle.
ui_patterns: personally-branded site design centered on the sitting PM's name/photo rather than an institutional identity
official-services disclaimer bar linking out to the umbrella belgium.be portal
high-contrast accessibility toggle exposed directly in the footer
minimal three-item top nav (Nieuws, Biografie, Contact) with almost no sub-menu
cross-link to a separate federal-government composition microsite (federale-regering.be) rather than embedding cabinet info
personal social-media icon row treated as primary header content, not relegated to the footer
Drupal 11 generator meta tag exposed in page source
four-language switcher (NL/FR/DE/EN) reflecting Belgium's three official languages plus English

bodies.name: Police.be / Police Fédérale (Belgian Integrated Police)
bodies.layout: A clean, service-oriented Drupal portal (theme-color meta confirms #004d9f) built around a single high-priority action: reporting to police. A cookie-consent modal covers the page on first load. Below it, a slim NL/FR/DE/EN language bar and a link out to the belgium.be umbrella portal precede a bold red-toned 'Demandez 101' emergency-call banner. The body opens with a 'digital counter' CTA for non-urgent declarations, followed by two feature cards ('Avis de recherche' / Wanted notices and 'Un job à la police?' recruitment), then a full-width 'Ma Police Locale' geolocation module letting citizens find their nearest local police zone by city or postal code, and a 'Police Fédérale' feature card. The footer lists statistics, an explainer on the two-tier 'Police Intégrée' (Integrated Police) structure, the Permanent Commission of the Local Police, and communication-campaign archives.
ui_patterns: prominent emergency-hotline call-to-action banner ('Demandez 101 une assistance policière urgente') fixed near the top
geolocation-based 'find your nearest local police zone' tool with postal-code fallback input
non-urgent digital reporting counter CTA (my.police.be) distinguished from the emergency hotline
explainer link on the two-tier federal/local 'Police Intégrée' governance structure
wanted-notices ('Avis de recherche') treated as a top-level homepage feature card, not buried in menu
recruitment microsite cross-link (jobpol.be) surfaced as a homepage card
granular cookie-consent modal with 'essential only' vs 'accept all' choices on every visit
four-language switcher (NL/FR/DE/EN) matching Belgium's federal linguistic structure
